channel.title: Suchetana Bauri — Blog
channel.description: Writing on AI enablement, communication and design by Suchetana Bauri.

item.title: Human in the loop is not an approval policy
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: An approval button records a decision; it does not prove anyone understood it. How to decide which agent actions need judgement, what reviewers must check, and whether the check works.

item.title: The coordination tax: why faster tasks do not always make faster organisations
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: AI can shorten the step, but most of the delay sits between the steps. Dickens, Adam Smith, the dynamo and 2026 data on where work waits, with a free handoff and delay-mapping workbook.

item.title: Your AI prototype works. Who will keep it working in 2027?
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: Small businesses can now build their own software with AI. Before depending on it, decide who owns it, what happens when it fails and whether it saves more work than it creates.

item.title: Your website has a second audience: software acting for customers
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: AI assistants now read and act on websites for customers. How to design for that second audience without losing the first: clear terms, stopping points and an audit you can run.

item.title: In an AI-saturated market, proof is part of the brand
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: Why proof now belongs inside the brand: what changed in 2026, four examples, a claims-and-proof register, and what to test in 2027.

item.title: Your AI campaign won the click. Did it lose the customer?
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: AI-generated ads can win the click and still lose the customer. What the 2026 evidence says about attention, disclosure and trust in synthetic advertising.

item.title: Before the next AI announcement, answer the question
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: As organisations prepare their 2027 AI plans, employees are still trying to establish what the last announcement means for their work. Some need better…

item.title: The AI adoption dashboard is green. Is the work any better?
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: Usage figures show people are using AI. Before the 2027 investment round, ask which workflows deliver better results once checking, correction and human effort are counted.

item.title: Brand strategy for 2027: what 2026 is teaching us
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: AI can help a brand produce, personalise and appear everywhere. The harder task is remaining worth choosing. What the 2026 evidence suggests brands should prepare for next year.

item.title: From digital marketing to AI-first: beyond faster content
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: What I learned from AI marketing pioneers, and why the real improvement came from redesigning the work, not collecting more tools.

item.title: OpenPencil review: not another screen generator
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: I tested OpenPencil on my own design file. An AI agent cleared the contrast findings in seconds, and left the design-system decision behind them on my desk.

item.title: AI strategy: what is your business for now?
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: Lessons from Adobe, DBS and Arizona State University on changing what an organisation offers, how it works and what it must protect.

item.title: Your next AI agent should fix a broken workflow, not invent a new job
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: In 2026, enterprises are moving beyond AI that answers questions towards systems that investigate, recommend and act. The opportunity for 2027 is to resolve the work that keeps getting stuck.

item.title: Your AI strategy is quietly rewriting the rules of work
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: When AI enters performance reviews, hiring decisions and everyday expectations, a leadership message becomes something more consequential. Before 2027, organisations need to explain the bargain they are asking employees to accept.

item.title: The interface owes you an explanation
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: The foundational UI/UX thinkers who shape how I approach design, communication and AI: Norman, Nielsen, Shneiderman, Krug, Garrett, Rosenfeld and Morville.

item.title: I stopped asking AI to write my marketing. I started redesigning the work.
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: How moving from prompts to context, bounded agents and connected workflows changed my digital marketing practice, and why editorial judgement matters more, not less.

item.title: Before you change the logo, find out what people think you do
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: A rebrand should close the distance between what a business has become and what people understand it to be. That requires decisions about the business itself.

item.title: Thought leadership is not a writing problem
item.dc:creator: Suchetana Bauri
item.description: What translating research at ISB, specialist knowledge at ELMS and internal communication at Microsoft (via partner) taught me about turning expertise into something people can use.
